title: fix(jest-config): only warn about global-only options where they're actually ignored
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #13576. What is left there is all of one shape: Jest warns about an option that sits in the right place, or says nothing about one it throws away. Four causes.

**The config that supplies the global config was validated as a project config.** `readConfig` decided this itself, by comparing the project path with the directory of the root config. That misfires whenever the two differ but the config is the same file:

- A project directory without its own config resolves, by traversal, to the root config. With `projects: ['<rootDir>/packages/*']` and one package that has no `jest.config.js`, the root config's own `bail`/`passWithNoTests`/… came back as `not supported in an individual project configuration. Move it to the root configuration.` They were already in the root configuration.
- With `jest --projects a b` and no `--config`, `readConfigs` takes the global config from the first project, so its global options really do drive the run — `testFailureExitCode: 7` in `a` gives exit code 7, the same option in `b` is ignored. Jest warned anyway, and pointed at a root config that does not exist.

`readConfigs` is the only place that knows which config supplied the global config, so it now decides and passes that down instead of `readConfig` guessing from path shapes.

**`reporters`, `coverageReporters` and `workerIdleMemoryLimit` were accepted per project and silently dropped.** They were in `ProjectConfig` and in the project schema, but every consumer reads them off the global config. They cannot be per-project as things stand — runners are keyed by `runner` + `runnerOptions` rather than by project, coverage is one aggregated map, and the reporters are a single pipeline — so they leave the project surface and warn like every other global-only option.

**`cwd` and `runnerOptions` type-checked in a project config and then warned.** They were in `InitialProjectOptions` only so that `Pick<..., keyof ProjectConfig>` resolved. Both are computed during normalization, so they are gone from the project type.

**`maxWorkers` and `coverageThreshold` in a project config produced no warning at all.** `maxWorkers` took the `allowsMultipleTypes` branch in `_validate` before the example config was consulted, so it never reached the unknown-option path. `coverageThreshold` is in the recursive denylist, which suppresses the unknown-option report as well as the recursion the entry is there for — and that entry only means something when the option exists in the schema, so a project config no longer carries it.

Two notes for review:

- Typing the two example configs in `ValidConfig.ts` as `Required<...>` changes nothing today, and turns "option added to the types but forgotten in the schema" — #16224 — into a compile error.
- Dropping the `parsedConfigs[0].globalConfig` fallback is breaking, so it is a `TODO` for the next major rather than part of this PR. The shape I would go for: read the global config from `process.cwd()` when several projects are passed without `--config`, the way the `argv.config` branch already does.

The docs list of root-only options was wrong in both directions, so it is rewritten here and in the 30.4/30.5 versioned copies — those releases ignore the same options, they just do it quietly.

## Test plan

- `packages/jest-config/src/__tests__/normalize.test.ts`: each newly global-only option (`reporters`, `coverageReporters`, `workerIdleMemoryLimit`, `coverageThreshold`, `maxWorkers`) warns once in a project config.
- `packages/jest-validate/src/__tests__/validate.test.ts`: `maxWorkers` is reported as unknown when the example config does not declare it, and still throws on the wrong type when it does.
- `e2e/__tests__/multiProjectRunner.test.ts`: a root config that a project resolves back to emits no warning; with `--projects p1 p2` and no root config, only `p2` is warned about while `p1`'s `testFailureExitCode` still applies.

```
yarn jest packages/jest-config packages/jest-core packages/jest-reporters packages/jest-runner packages/jest-validate packages/test-utils
yarn jest e2e/__tests__/multiProjectRunner e2e/__tests__/showConfig
yarn typecheck:tests
yarn lint
```

Manual check, with `packages/a` having no config of its own:

```js
// jest.config.js
module.exports = {
  bail: 1,
  passWithNoTests: true,
  projects: ["<rootDir>/packages/a", "<rootDir>/packages/b"],
};
```

Before: three validation warnings, for `projects`, `bail` and `passWithNoTests`. After: none.
